items.title: How brands should craft their AI strategies—GEO and AEO tips for marketers
items.summary: Brands need to analyze the AI landscape and prioritize platforms like YouTube or Reddit where their buyers are active to optimize for generative engine optimization (GEO) and answer engine optimization (AEO), which involve shaping how AI platforms cite and describe brands. GEO relies on foundational SEO practices since LLMs conduct traditional searches, but emphasizes fresh content under 13 weeks old and readable URLs to influence citations. Additionally, brands should optimize for AI agents by ensuring feeds and APIs are accessible, as LLMs increasingly act on behalf of consumers, and video content, especially on YouTube, is becoming crucial for visibility.

items.title: AEO vs GEO in 2026: Key Differences and Strategic Applications
items.summary: Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) focuses on optimizing content for direct answers in featured snippets, answer boxes, and voice assistants, targeting factual queries with concise, structured formats and schema markup. Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) aims to ensure brands are cited in AI-generated summaries from tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity AI, emphasizing in-depth, original content with entity signals and expert insights for exploratory queries. Both strategies complement each other in an AI-first search landscape, with AEO securing quick visibility and GEO building long-term authority through citations.

items.title: As brands respond to AI search era, paid and organic are merging
items.summary: For nearly 20 years, paid search and SEO have been separate disciplines, but as brands adapt to the zero-click search era driven by AI features like Google’s Overviews, marketing agencies are breaking down barriers between organic and paid teams. Agencies such as Digitas and Barkley OKRP are aligning teams around shared client goals, integrating SEO expertise into keyword bidding strategies and using organic insights to optimize against AI summaries. This convergence is supported by tools like Adthena’s AI Overview Index and new solutions from agencies like Assembly, enabling joint data sharing and holistic approaches to maintain competitiveness in AI-disrupted search landscapes.

items.title: How to increase Google Discover traffic with technical fixes
items.summary: The article outlines technical optimizations for Google Discover, including verifying the Discover publisher profile to ensure proper linking of website and social profiles, using large images with a minimum width of 1,200 pixels and proper Open Graph tags, and enhancing publisher and author transparency through clear bylines, bios, and schema markup. It emphasizes that Discover favors timely, relevant content from authoritative sources, and while traffic is declining due to increased social posts and AI summaries, these fixes can improve visibility without harming traditional search. Good content remains essential, and optimizations like max-image-preview:large tags and Organization schema support overall performance in Discover.

items.title: AIOSEO Changelog: New AI-Powered Keyword Report Tool
items.summary: AIOSEO has launched AI Insights, a new AI-powered Keyword Report tool that reveals which brands rank in AI search results, now free for a limited time. This update helps users track and optimize for AI search visibility. Additional fixes include improved TruSEO analysis and redirect import enhancements.

items.title: Publishers sue 'shadow' library allegedly powering AI chatbots
items.summary: A group of major publishers including the Big Five English-language houses and others like Cengage and Elsevier filed a lawsuit in New York federal court on March 6, 2026, against Anna's Archive, accusing it of pirating over 63 million books and providing access to AI developers for training models. The suit alleges the site, run anonymously since 2022, violates prior court orders and seeks site shutdown plus up to $150,000 damages per work. This action underscores growing conflicts over pirated content fueling AI development.

items.title: Jeff Lemire signs five-book deal with HarperCollins’ Harper Alley imprint
items.summary: Comic book creator Jeff Lemire has inked a five-book deal with HarperCollins' Harper Alley imprint, beginning with the three-volume supernatural detective series Mr. Oblivion illustrated by Teddy Kristiansen. The deal also includes two standalone graphic novels, one illustrated by Charlie Adlard. The first volume, Incantations, is scheduled for release in summer 2027.

items.title: Parents awarded $1.5M after Supreme Court win in LGBTQ+ books case
items.summary: A group of conservative religious parents successfully sued the Montgomery County Board of Education in Maryland after it refused opt-outs for classes featuring LGBTQ+-themed books such as Pride Puppy! and My Rainbow, claiming violation of religious rights. The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in their favor on February 27, 2026, leading to a $1.5 million settlement requiring parental notifications and opt-out permissions. The case highlights tensions over curriculum content in public schools.

items.title: A.I. editorial feedback is getting better. But should you use it?
items.summary: Literary agent Nathan Bransford experimented with Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 model for editorial feedback on his screenplay, finding it provides effective plot guidance but often flattens unique writing styles. He warns against over-reliance, particularly for inexperienced writers, amid publishing industry resistance including calls for AI disclosure and rejection of assisted submissions. The post, dated March 2, 2026, debates the ethics and utility of AI in writing and editing.

items.title: Publishing Ethics Clash With AI Book Flood On Kindle
items.summary: The Authors Guild is calling for visible labeling of AI-generated books and royalty sharing when AI quotes full texts on platforms like Kindle amid a flood of low-quality AI content. The Publishers Association demands faster takedowns of infringing AI books. The story, published about 5 days ago, addresses ethical concerns in self-publishing flooded by AI.

items.title: Marlon Wayans unveils first trailer for raucous 'rebooquel' 'Scary Movie 6' (exclusive)
items.summary: Marlon Wayans and his brothers Shawn and Keenen Ivory Wayans return to the Scary Movie franchise after 25 years with Scary Movie 6, described as a 'rebooquel' that combines reboot elements with a new installment, reuniting with stars Anna Faris and Regina Hall. The trailer spoofs recent horror films like Heart Eyes, M3GAN, Scream, Weapons, and Terrifier, featuring meta-humor, equal-opportunity offense, and jokes about cancel culture, safe spaces, and pronouns. The film is set for release in theaters on June 5th.

items.title: ‘Game of Thrones’ Movie Officially in the Works at Warner Bros. From ‘Andor’ Writer
items.summary: Warner Bros. is developing a movie set in the Game of Thrones universe, focusing on the story of King Aegon I Targaryen’s conquest of Westeros, with writer Beau Willimon attached. This film project is separate from an early-stage series version of the same story in development at HBO. The news follows a tease in a recent Hollywood Reporter profile of George R.R. Martin.

items.title: Despite Backlash, Bad Bunny's Super Bowl Halftime Show Sets Global Viewership Record with 4.157 Billion Views in 24 Hours
items.summary: Bad Bunny performed at Super Bowl LX on February 8, 2026, featuring high-energy reggaeton hits, guest appearances from artists like J Balvin and Rosalía, and references to Puerto Rico's colonial history and Latino experiences. The show achieved 4.157 billion global views in 24 hours despite backlash from conservative commentators criticizing the use of Spanish lyrics without subtitles and perceived political overtones. Online polls showed a split in opinions, with some viewers expressing dissatisfaction.

items.title: ‘Scary Movie’ Shifts Release to Early June, Will Now Open Opposite ‘Masters of the Universe’
items.summary: The sixth film in the Scary Movie franchise has moved its theatrical release from June 12 to June 5 following a positive response to its trailer. Marlon Wayans, who wrote, produces, and stars in the film, announced the date change, noting the excitement as the movie will compete with other films. The comedy features a cast including Shawn Wayans, Regina Hall, and Anna Faris.

items.title: Box Office: 'Hoppers' Opening To $40M, 'Bride' Bombing With $8M-$10M
items.summary: Pixar’s original animated film Hoppers opened to approximately $40M in the U.S. and Canada, marking the studio’s strongest debut for an original since Coco, driven by positive word of mouth and an A CinemaScore. In contrast, Warner Bros.’ The Bride!, a period horror film with an $80M budget, underperformed with $8M-$10M and a C+ CinemaScore amid mixed social media reactions criticizing the script and pacing. The disparity highlights differing audience reception for family animation versus horror.

items.title: Timothée Chalamet Faces Backlash From Ballet and Opera Communities After Viral 'No One Cares' Comment
items.summary: Timothée Chalamet triggered backlash from ballet and opera communities after dismissing the art forms by saying 'no one cares' about them in a viral interview comment. Performing arts groups responded by inviting him to events to change his mind, while online discussions highlighted the controversy. The Oscar-nominated actor's remarks sparked debate on the relevance of classical performing arts.

items.title: How a woman founder is using AI to help small businesses innovate
items.summary: Romanian entrepreneur Catalina Banuleasa has created Idea Morph, a web-based platform that uses AI to provide guided frameworks for collaborative ideation, enabling small businesses to generate ideas, analyze customer needs, and develop new products and services more efficiently. Supported by Mastercard Strive, the platform offers free access to structured ideation, AI-powered insights, and collaborative tools, helping small businesses create business plans, pricing strategies, and marketing campaigns without large teams or budgets. AI-powered tools like Idea Morph help entrepreneurs structure ideas, test them quickly, and make decisions with greater clarity and confidence.

items.title: Intuit is betting its 40 years of small business data can outlast the SaaSpocalypse
items.summary: Intuit faces market challenges from AI agents that automate bookkeeping, tax filing, and accounting tasks, potentially disrupting its per-seat subscription model with service-as-a-service offerings. The company counters by leveraging 40 years of first-party and third-party data from 100 million customers, deep small business expertise, and integrations like a multi-year partnership with Anthropic to deploy specialized AI agents via Intuit Intelligence for finance tasks.
